## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 6.2.3) is a section of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. Within the structural architecture of the *Yamaka*, this text belongs to the process division (*pavattivāra*), which systematically investigates phenomena through three primary analytical lenses: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and simultaneous origination and cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Anderson 1999; Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. In this section, paired catechisms analyze the arising and ceasing of doctrinal categories across time—evaluating conditions in the present, past, and future, particularly with respect to persons and planes of rebirth [Nyanatiloka 2007; Anderson 1999]. Modern scholars note that the *Yamaka*'s *pavattivāra* sections, including the *uppādanirodhavāra*, represent an early milestone in Buddhist process metaphysics and the development of the theory of momentariness, introducing the subdivision of a moment (*khaṇa*) into distinct moments of origination and destruction (*uppādakkhaṇa*, *bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005].
